abstract: Epigenetic clocks based on bulk blood DNA methylation are powerful tools for quantifying biological aging, but bulk measurements conflate cell-autonomous epigenetic changes with age-related shifts in blood cell composition. Here, we develop LongReadClock, a set of cell-type-resolved epigenetic aging clocks constructed from cohort-scale long-read whole-genome sequencing of bulk blood without physical cell sorting. Individual sequencing reads were classified using seven target-specific blood-cell models using methylation-based log-likelihood-ratio scoring against a purified-cell atlas. LongReadClock achieved mean absolute errors of 2.8-5.7 years on held-out samples across bulk blood and digitally resolved cell types. Covariate-adjusted analyses identified associations that differed across cell types, including lower mean epigenetic age deviation (EAD) in males in B-cell and NK-cells, associations of systolic blood pressure and resting heart rate with myeloid EAD, and higher NK-cell EAD in participants with asthma. A Fisher-information screen was used to prioritize age-informative genomic windows and to explore read-level methylation patterns at the ELOVL2 locus. These results support cell-type-resolved epigenetic age inference from cohort-scale long-read methylation data from standard bulk blood samples.
